assumptions: the case is escalated: the request says escalating it, and the later 'Also, escalate case CS-0000030' implies this case is escalated too
escalation_reason breach_risk kept from the benchmark check: the request asks that no breach occur, and the policy allows escalation when SLA breach risk exists

requirements.text: applying the SLA Resolution - Critical, ensuring no breach occurs

assumptions: SLA Resolution - Critical is sla_def 6; the seed already links it to case 32 as row 64, paused while the case is pending
applied to a case now in progress the SLA must run, so stage is in_progress; the policy pauses SLAs only while the case is pending
has_breached 0 because the request asks that no breach occur
selected by case and SLA definition: the running row may be a new link or row 64 resumed, and exactly one must run
disagreement: kind: A change, B create; chose create because the requirement asks that one running row exist whichever row it is, and the benchmark's check reads the step as a new link

New SLA has been linked to the case.evidence: case 32 already has SLA Resolution - Critical linked on the seed (case_sla 64, paused), so the count is 1 before the agent acts, and a fresh link would make it 2 and fail; the requirement that carries it tests one running, unbreached row instead

check entitlement details.evidence: entitlement 11 (account 2, product 202) is already active on the seed; the request asks for no entitlement change, and the policy only asks for the entitlement to be verified, which writes nothing

notes:
Three benchmark checks read a cell rather than count rows (case 32's assignment group and assignee, case 47's state); their requirements test the same values as counts. Case 47's closed_on is a server-kept timestamp and is not tested.
The SLA requirement is the main judgement: the benchmark counts any link of SLA 6 to case 32, which the seed already holds, so the requirement asks for exactly one running, unbreached link instead.
Case 32's escalation is a judgement: 'We need to rapidly address this before escalation' could argue against escalating, but 'escalating it' with 'ensuring no breach occurs' and the following 'Also, escalate case CS-0000030' read as an escalation for breach risk, as the benchmark tests.
The policy asks for escalation justifications in case notes; the schema has no case-notes table, so they are untestable. Amelia Jones's phone is not given and is not a cell. The SLAs already linked to cases 30 and 47 are not tested: the request says nothing about them.
The opening sentence about Zebra Partners' several critical cases names no action beyond the ones that follow, so no stay is written for the account's other critical pending cases (48, 49), which are on other products.
disagreement: value: the kind of the SLA requirement on case 32: change in one pass, create in the other; chose create, as recorded on the requirement.
disagreement: form: one pass tests case 32's state and escalation, and case 30's escalation and state, as separate requirements, the other as one requirement per case with the same cells and sources; kept them separate because the request asks for each as its own step, so a failure names the step that was missed.
